name: Birsha
title: Pharaoh who met Abraham
summary: Birsha (also known as Bera) was the king of Sodom during Abraham's time. He was one of the five kings in the Jordan Valley who rebelled against King Chedorlaomer of Elam and were defeated in the Valley of Siddim. After Abraham rescued the captives and plunder from Chedorlaomer's army, Birsha offered Abraham the spoils of war, but Abraham refused.

keyEvents.title: Rebellion against Chedorlaomer
keyEvents.description: Birsha, the king of Sodom, was among five kings in the Jordan Valley who served Chedorlaomer for twelve years but rebelled in the thirteenth year.

keyEvents.title: Defeat in the Valley of Siddim
keyEvents.description: Birsha and his allies were defeated by Chedorlaomer and his confederates in the Valley of Siddim. Birsha and the king of Gomorrah fled and fell into tar pits in the valley.

keyEvents.title: Captives taken from Sodom
keyEvents.description: After the defeat, the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah were plundered, and the inhabitants, including Lot, were taken captive.

keyEvents.title: Abraham's Rescue Mission
keyEvents.description: Abraham gathered 318 men, pursued Kedorlaomer's army, defeated them, and brought back all the captives and all the plunder, including Lot.

keyEvents.title: Birsja Meets Abraham After the Victory
keyEvents.description: After his victory over Kedorlaomer, Birsja went out to meet Abraham in the Valley of Shaveh (the King's Valley). Birsja asked Abraham to return the people but let him keep the plunder for himself.

keyEvents.title: Abraham Refuses Birsja's Offer
keyEvents.description: Abraham refused to accept anything from Birsja and swore by the Lord that he would not take so much as a thread or a sandal strap, so that Birsja could not say, 'I have made Abraham rich.'
